historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun's Muqaddimah, written in the 14th century CE, mentions a woman named Afizah bint Abd al-Rahman as a notable figure in the history of the Hafsid dynasty in Tunisia. She was a powerful vizier and later the regent for her young son during his reign. The Hafsid dynasty ruled Tunisia from the 13th to the 16th century CE, making Afizah a significant figure in Islamic history during this period.

Al-Maqrizi's 'Ittiqad al-Sadid', written in the late 15th century CE, recounts the life of a woman named Afizah bint al-Hajjaj, a Sufi saint who lived in Egypt during the Mamluk Sultanate. She was a prominent figure in the Sufi community and is revered for her spiritual achievements. The Mamluk Sultanate ruled Egypt and Syria from the 13th to the 16th century CE, making Afizah an important figure in Islamic history during this period.
